# Virelo

Virelo is a private video library for files a user already owns. It presents local folders through a streaming-style interface with search, favorites, watch progress, folder queues, details, and a Shorts-style feed.

Official site: https://virelo.riyo.me/
Setup guide: https://virelo.riyo.me/setup
Web player: https://virelo.riyo.me/app
Web source: https://github.com/VireloHQ/Virelo-Web
CLI source: https://github.com/VireloHQ/Virelo
npm package: https://www.npmjs.com/package/virelo

## Privacy model

The Virelo web player reads only folders selected by the user through browser file APIs. Selected video files are not uploaded to Virelo, copied to a hosted library, or sent to a third party. Library state such as favorites, settings, thumbnails, and watch progress is stored locally in the browser.

The browser-only web player needs no account. The CLI server is a separate application: Virelo 0.4+ requires sign-in. On first launch, create the administrator account using localhost on the device running the server. Administrators can add users and set library access and permissions in Account Manager.

## Web player

Open https://virelo.riyo.me/app and choose a folder. The browser builds the library on the device without installation. Supported browsers can optionally add Virelo to the home screen as a PWA. Browser file-system support varies, so users should use a current browser that supports directory selection.

## CLI quick start

Open a terminal in a folder containing videos and run:

    npx virelo

Choose another media folder explicitly:

    npx virelo --media ~/Videos

On a trusted local network, expose the library to another device with:

    npx virelo --host 0.0.0.0

Do not expose a Virelo instance directly to the public internet. The LAN mode is intended for trusted private networks.

## Supported environments

The CLI requires stable Node.js 22.23.4+, 24.22.1+ or 26.12.1+ within those release lines. The browser-only player does not require Node.js on the user's device.

The Virelo CLI setup guide covers Windows, macOS, Linux, and Android through Termux. Optional FFmpeg and ffprobe support enables codec probing, thumbnails, and HLS fallback for formats a browser cannot play directly.

## Main features

- Browse videos through Home, Library, Details, Player, and Shorts views.
- Search selected folders and mark videos as favorites.
- Resume videos from saved watch progress.
- Save named playlists, reorder videos, shuffle and edit horizontal or vertical queues.
- Browse with an Explorer folder tree, address completion and customizable display names without renaming source folders.
- Reduce loudness differences with optional live volume leveling. It is not full-file integrated LUFS normalization and is unavailable on Safari/iOS WebKit.
- Choose four controller styles, accent colors and English, Japanese, Simplified Chinese, Korean or Russian.
- Play portrait clips in a responsive Shorts-style feed.
- Keep selected files and library state on the user's device.

## Self-hosted features

The CLI server can automatically match movie and series information and cache posters, backdrops and episode artwork. This is not available in the browser-only player. Filename queries or media identifiers may be sent to metadata providers; source video files are not uploaded to them.

Each server account has its own playlists, favorites, watch progress and appearance preferences. Administrators control library access and operation permissions, send private in-app announcements and can enable visibly disclosed activity monitoring. Monitoring is off by default and requires the current notice to be acknowledged. None of these administrative features exist in the browser-only player.

## Help and source

Use the setup guide for commands and troubleshooting. Report reproducible web player problems at https://github.com/VireloHQ/Virelo-Web/issues and CLI problems at https://github.com/VireloHQ/Virelo/issues. Do not attach private media, local file paths, account credentials, or browser storage.
